podcast.title: Early 90s Mention
podcast.body: Math rock was mentioned as one of the many forms of Alt Rock that enjoyed moments in the sun during the 90s, indicating the genre's niche but significant presence in the diverse alternative landscape. "We could have just as well mentioned, early emo, dream pop, math rock, post-hardcore, alt metal, alt country, Tweet Rock, contemporary Christian alternative music, and so many more."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Overlap with Post-Rock
podcast.body: Math rock can overlap with post-rock, but it is typically very challenging to play due to its complicated and precise nature, demanding a lot of precision. "Math rock can overlap with post-rock. This is music that's very challenging to play because it's so complicated and precise. It requires a lot of precision."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What Exactly is Post Rock? Part 2

podcast.title: Pillar Established by Spiderland
podcast.body: *Spiderland* by Slint is consecrated as a pillar of the Math Rock genre, profoundly influencing its development and recognition within the music scene. "y se consagrará como el pilar del mat rock."

srcs.episode: Spiderland: La Revolución del Rock Hecha por Adolescentes

podcast.title: Pre-2010s Presence and 2010s Comeback
podcast.body: Math Rock, characterized by its complicated, complex, and "impossible to dance to" nature, had a fair amount of presence prior to the 2010s, inspired by masters like Rush, King Crimson, and Yes. In the 2010s, it saw a comeback as part of a broader progressive rock resurgence, with bands using eight or nine-string guitars to achieve complex sounds. "Now to be fair, we saw a fair amount of what was known as math rock in the arts." "This was complicated, complex, hard to play, and impossible to dance to rock, inspired by masters like Russian, King Crimson, and yes."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 4: The Revivals

podcast.title: Structural Philosophy
podcast.body: Math rock focuses on building complicated structures, in contrast to post-rock's emphasis on long, flowing fields of sound. "Math rock is about building complicated structures. Post-rock is about long flowing fields."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What Exactly is Post Rock? Part 2

podcast.title: Time Signatures and Tension
podcast.body: A key difference from post-rock is math rock's preference for weird time signatures, in contrast to post-rock's smooth beats (almost always 4/4, occasionally 6/8). Math rock songs often feature significant tension, arising from their angularity and the physicality of the playing. "A big difference is that math rock loves weird timesignatures. Post-rock tends to prefer smooth beats, almost always 4-4, but 6-8 comes up once in a while."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What Exactly is Post Rock? Part 2
